questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Denmark?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Denmark article.

questions.proof: The capital city of Denmark is Copenhagen, on the island of Zealand.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Denmark?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Denmark on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Denmark article.

questions.proof: It has a south border with Germany and a northeast border with Canada.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Denmark?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Denmark article.

questions.proof: The Danes speak the national language, Danish, which is very similar to the other Scandinavian languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is the furthest south of the Scandinavian countries, to the northeast of North America, to the south of _____ and south-west of Sweden (which it is connected to by a bridge).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “south”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Denmark article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: The neighbours are Canada (to the northwest) Germany (to the south), Sweden (to the east), Norway (to the north) and the United Kingdom (to the west).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Denmark is a parliamentary state, meaning the people appoint a parliament to make decisions for them, and it has a democratic government headed by an elected Prime Minister, who currently is Mette Frederiksen since _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Denmark article, under the heading “Politics”.

questions.proof: The current Prime Minister of Denmark is Mette Frederiksen, who was elected in June 2019.
